A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PromptLoop, with matching core methods and experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-alignment experiments, component ablations and qualitative analyses in Tables 2–4, Figure 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original baseline comparisons, runtime measurements, transfer experiments and prompt-behavior analyses.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix E.1 introduces an inference adaptation that converts flow-matching timesteps into diffusion timesteps with equivalent SNR before supplying them to the policy. The core MDP, GRPO training, sparse refinement and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The named prompt datasets and alignment tasks remain Pick-a-Pic v2, RePrompt prompts and GenEval; the new generator configurations do not establish new data coverage. However, v2 Appendix C.4 introduces DanceGRPO training on its unspecified 'official' dataset, so the PDFs cannot establish whether this adds different represented data.

E2.justification: v2 adds GPT-5 to the single- and composite-reward comparisons and DanceGRPO to the SD1.5 composability experiment (Tables 1–2). DanceGRPO was only discussed as prior work in v1. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark protocols are retained, but substantial new evaluation settings are introduced: inference timing on one A100 with batch size 8, BERTScore and LLM-based intent recall, FLUX.1-dev and SD3.5-large configurations, and a Qwen3-VL-4B policy ablation. DanceGRPO additionally uses 50 training epochs with HPSv2 reward.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and refinement-step ablations, v2 tests prompt-length growth, semantic drift, interpretability of early denoised feedback, training stability and stronger policy initialization (Appendices D.2–D.3 and E.2–E.3). Runtime profiling also directly examines the cost of additional refinement steps.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 11 explicitly reports average token counts with standard-deviation bands. v1 already contains shaded bands in Figure 6, which are retained, but lacks this explicitly identified variability statistic. No additional repeated-run counts, seeds or significance tests are specified.

E6.justification: All original score rows in v1 Tables 2–4 are retained in v2 Tables 1–3. Added results include GPT-5 and DanceGRPO comparisons, flow-matching transfer scores, runtime measurements and new diagnostic curves. Table 7 reports ImageReward 0.6922 with Qwen3-VL-4B versus 0.6320 with Qwen2.5-VL-3B, explicitly comparing different policy configurations.

T1.justification: The substantive diffusion equations, MDP definitions, GRPO objective and denoised-estimate formulation are retained. Correcting the sampled-action index in prose makes it consistent with the existing definition; no substantive theorem, proof or derivation is added.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit contribution claim of negligible or minimal additional inference overhead in the abstract and introduction. The central claims concerning reward optimization, generalization, composability and mitigation of reward hacking remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations attributing prompt-length differences to generator capability, intent preservation to original-prompt conditioning and episodic rewards, and training stability to initialization, LoRA and a fixed environment. It also explains early denoised-state usefulness and argues that relative policy overhead decreases with larger generators.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses approximately three days per training run, the GPT-5 model snapshot, DanceGRPO training and code information, and the models used for semantic-recall evaluation. Existing GRPO, LoRA, hardware, resizing and prompting details remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Idea2Img to related work and references supporting denoised-state evaluation, flow-matching backbones and semantic scoring, including Free2Guide and BERTScore. Its central positioning relative to weight-level alignment and existing prompt-refinement approaches is retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are preserved. Changes include adding PromptLoop to the title, terminology and grammar corrections, an acknowledgment, and reorganizing the former additional-results appendix into prompt-evolution and additional-results sections.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint layout to two columns. The original MDP comparison table is incorporated into Figure 3, Figure 2 gains a preference/runtime panel, and GPT-5 columns expand comparison grids. New runtime, transfer and initialization tables and Figures 11–14 substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support for practicality and reliability: v1 lacks direct runtime and semantic-drift measurements, while v2 adds these alongside training diagnostics and transfer to flow-matching models. These address important validation gaps while retaining the original results. The 'negligible overhead' wording is overstated relative to Table 4's approximately 23% increase at five refinements, but the overall gain in evidence is substantial.
